cases.note: Missing a required positive property yields a provenance-valid DENY, not ALLOW.
All required positive properties are present and the decision is ALLOW.
Deleting required evidence may remove ALLOW; it must not manufacture ALLOW.
A DENY to ALLOW transition under evidence deletion violates monotonicity.
Negative evidence cannot be discarded to produce ALLOW.
Removing stale evidence cannot transform DENY into ALLOW.
Conflicting evidence cannot be silently collapsed into ALLOW.
Material policy identity changed while the decision identity was reused.
A mutable latest policy locator is not an immutable policy identity.
A decision cannot claim provenance while omitting the decisive evidence identities.
Declared policy identity and evaluated policy bytes must agree.
Decision evaluation outside the policy validity interval is invalid.
An expired decision cannot silently re-enter the current evidence/decision state.
Exact replay of identical decision material is idempotent and remains provenance-preserving.
Conflicting policy outcomes remain unresolved rather than selecting a winner.
A quorum threshold remains a composition fact and is not an authorization grant.
A policy decision must not be represented as scientific truth.
A policy decision must not be represented as civic authority.
Decision semantics cannot depend on evidence arrival order.
Omitting policy identity must not convert a DENY into ALLOW or create an unverifiable decision.
Deleting irrelevant evidence leaves the decision unchanged.
